title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Control flow means deciding which step runs next. What is the core difference between a workflow and an agent?

options.text: An agent can call tools, while a workflow cannot call any
An agent runs on a larger model than a workflow does
In a workflow code picks each step; in an agent the model does
An agent takes several steps, while a workflow takes just one

items.stem: Your booking feature always runs check_calendar, then reserve_slot, then one model call that writes the confirmation message. Is this a workflow or an agent?

options.text: An agent, because a model writes part of the output
A workflow, because the code fixes the order of the steps
An agent, because it calls tools such as check_calendar
An agent, because it runs more than one step per request

items.stem: A fixed workflow makes 2 model calls per request. An agent doing the same job averages 5 model calls per request. Over 200 requests, how many more model calls does the agent make?
Which request is best handled by an agent, because the steps needed cannot be listed ahead of time?

options.text: "Reserve the 3D printer for Friday at 2 pm."
"Show me all of my current bookings."
"Remind me an hour before my booking starts."
"Why are my acrylic cuts melting at the edges?"

items.stem: One model call labels each student message "booking", "manual question" or "other". Code then runs a fixed handler for that label. Is this a workflow or an agent?

options.text: A workflow, because code runs fixed paths and the model only labels
An agent, because the model's label decides which path runs
An agent, because the model makes a decision during the run
An agent, because it calls the model before any handler runs

items.stem: The makerspace assistant must book machines (check calendar, reserve, confirm) and answer open-ended questions about the manuals. In one sentence, which part would you build as a fixed workflow, and why?
